question_text: A hypothetical metal alloy has a grain diameter of $1.7 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~mm}$. After a heat treatment at $450^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ for 250 min the grain diameter has increased to $4.5 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~mm}$. Compute the time required for a specimen of this same material (i.e., $d{0}=1.7 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~mm}$ ) to achieve a grain diameter of $8.7 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~mm}$ while being heated at $450^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Assume the $n$ grain diameter exponent has a value of 2.1.The unit of the answer is min.
response:
The grain-growth law is $d^n - d_0^n = Kt$. Using the first heat treatment to find $K$, then solving for the time to reach $d = 8.7\times10^{-2}$ mm:

$$t_2 = \frac{d_2^n - d_0^n}{d_1^n - d_0^n}\,t_1 \approx 1109.4 \text{ min}$$

$$\boxed{1109.4}$$
